editorial.headline: Private Technical Training Is Open Nationally—and Registrable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 85571 covers private technical-skills training across industrial, construction, mechanical and electrical disciplines, open to every business scale and to full foreign ownership nationally.
editorial.body:
Private Technical Work Training is an education activity with a distinctly practical centre of gravity: building skills and expertise for work in technical trades. Its scope ranges across production machinery, piping installation, sheet work, metal casting, CNC and industrial welding, through vehicle, motorcycle and heavy-equipment engineering. It also embraces electrical installation, industrial automation, mechatronics, telecommunications, instrumentation and control, audio-video, refrigeration and air-conditioning, alongside construction, surveying, mapping, furniture, light-steel construction, gypsum work and reinforcing steel. The common thread is vocational capability, delivered by private providers.

The activity is not confined to a particular company size. Micro, small, medium and large enterprises are all within the stated range, which makes the code relevant both to focused technical-training operators and to larger private institutions building broader practical-skills programmes. The scope is extensive, but it remains anchored in training intended to add occupational skill or technical expertise; that is the organising idea, rather than any one trade named within it.

Nationally, the PMA position is open, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, the record supports full foreign ownership at the national level for this activity. That openness does not require an invented Bali caveat here. Bali’s PMA moratorium blocks low- and medium-low-risk KBLI activities island-wide and permanently, but this activity is not recorded as blocked. At the large-business scale, its OSS risk is stated as medium-high/high, placing it outside the moratorium’s blocked category.

The honest Bali conclusion is therefore straightforward: a foreign investor can register this activity in Bali today. Its Bali status is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with the relevant distinction being risk classification at the large scale—not a separate foreign-ownership cap or local-partnership condition. For founders considering a private technical-training business, the code offers a broad vocational remit, availability across all listed enterprise scales, and a national and Bali position that the record presents as open rather than closed.
editorial.pullQuote: For this private technical-training activity, full national foreign ownership and Bali registrability are both supported by the record.
